data_model_notes: This is Bob Zybach's own data model, preserved: an interview (tour) is divided into Parts of about 47 minutes, each Part being one cassette side; segments are his indexed stops, cited as map stop # / tape side / minute / topic / transcript page / (photo count).

Topic 1-4, Notes and Map-1/Map-2 are TAPE-level columns in the xlsx, not per-segment. They are carried on each tape and repeated on every segment of that tape as topics_1_4 / notes / map_refs; they are not aligned one-to-one with the segments and no alignment was invented.
The xlsx columns headed 1-6 (all 'X' or 'x') are undocumented in the file; their values are preserved verbatim in each tape's index_columns_1_6 and are not interpreted here.

minute, transcript_page_as_printed, stop_label_as_printed, topic, tape_label_as_printed and every *_as_printed field are verbatim from the source. transcript_page is null where the TOC prints '00' (the missing 45-minute segment, which has no transcript).

interviewer is 'Bob Zybach' for all six: stated in the TOC header ('Interviewer(s): Bob Zybach, with Amber Ross and Randy Wiest') and in the interview #1 and #4 paragraphs; the xlsx names 'Bob' first in every row.

mp3_url was matched by ORWW folder date + tape number + side and then verified against the served file: for all 27 indexed tapes Bob's MP3-MB column equals the file's Content-Length / 1e6 to within 0.1 MB (see each tape's mp3_match; sizes from the sibling record records/elliott/recordings.json, which also supplies mp3_recording_id).

participants are the first names exactly as Bob typed them in the five unheaded xlsx columns (leading/trailing spaces trimmed); interview #4's pair of 'Bob' entries is Bob Zybach and Bob Jacobson, and 'DavidG' appears once for David Gould.

interviews.route_description: Tape 1A. Interview with Jerry Phillips at his home in Coos Bay by Bob Zybach on October 6, 2017. The focus of this brief discussion was some of the peripheral characters in Phillips’ book Caulked Boots and Cheese Sandwiches. The interview was also conducted as a test of the relative quality of recording devices being considered for subsequent field trips. The digital recorder was tinny and difficult to work with, so this and following interviews were recorded on cassettes with a portable tape recorder. No photographs were taken during this interview.
